clue.text: Easy sports with beach teams, depending on circumstances

indicators.note: to sport can mean to play about, so the letters of the words around it frolic into a new order

explanation.surface: Relaxed games on the sand, with team line-ups decided by whatever the conditions happen to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports' reads as a noun for beach games but is the anagram signal for EASY and BEACH TEAMS together.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom used when a choice varies with the situation, so it is a phrase meaning contingent on circumstances.

clue.text: One indicates school dismissing head

indicators.note: dismissing the head means the opening letter of the school's name is dropped

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school in north-west London

explanation.surface: A school sends its headteacher packing, and one person points out what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a well-known English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer sign on a road or screen is the thing that shows direction, so it is something that indicates.

clue.text: Trip south involved in getting university job

indicators.note: involved here means tangled or complicated, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A complicated journey south is part of landing a post at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in getting' simply links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The post of a tutor, a teaching role at a university, is a university job.

clue.text: One guides journey uphill, stifling outraged cry

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so one piece is held inside the other
in a down clue going uphill means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a ride is a journey
fie is an old exclamation of disgust or outrage

explanation.surface: A guide on a climbing trek holds back an angry shout.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uphill' means read from the bottom up, giving EDIR; 'stifling' wraps that round the archaic exclamation of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who edifies instructs and improves others morally, so is a person who guides.

clue.text: A request taken up over criminal activity in teens or twenties?

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means the word is lifted and read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to beg is to request
a racket is a fraudulent or criminal scheme

explanation.surface: A plea is raised about some crime committed by young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns BEG into GEB; 'over' in a down clue just places the first part above RACKET.
explanation.definitionFit: The teens and twenties are examples of age ranges, hence the question mark marking definition by example.

clue.text: Bidder, perhaps, participating in sale as thought

indicators.note: participating in means the letters take part within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A buyer takes part in an auction, or so it was believed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bidder' suggests an auction, but it is a bridge player; East is one of the four seats at bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game bridge the four players are named by compass points, and each one bids.

clue.text: Medicine I start to require during a dizzy spell

indicators.note: during means within the period of, so these letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: a spin is a whirl or giddy turn

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A patient says they need medication while feeling giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus R (start of 'require') goes inside A SPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkilling drug, so it is a type of medicine.

clue.text: Bear book getting no success

parts.note: ruin is the opposite of success, total failure

explanation.surface: A book about a bear that fails to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional name for a brown bear in fable and folklore.

clue.text: People complaining about SF movie shops

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to rail is to complain bitterly, so railers are complainers
E.T. is Spielberg's science-fiction film

explanation.surface: Moviegoers grumble about a sci-fi film being sold in stores.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailers are businesses that sell goods to the public, and shops is a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Head of Pixar left out misguided cartoon character

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of the word that follows
misguided means led astray, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: The boss of an animation studio drops a badly conceived character.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's dog is a famous animated figure, so a cartoon character.

clue.text: Notice heads, with a couple changing places

indicators.note: a couple of letters swap positions, the V and S trading places

parts.note: the obverse is the heads side of a coin

explanation.surface: A coin's heads side is spotted, with two figures swapping seats.
explanation.walkthrough: The V and S of OBVERSE swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to perceive or see, matching notice used as a verb.

clue.text: Arriving, I will be mobbed by most of less competent fighters

indicators.note: mobbed by means crowded round by, so the other letters enclose these
most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: worse means less good or less able
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrival

explanation.surface: Someone arriving expects to be swarmed by poorer fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: Arr. is the railway timetable shorthand; 'most of' drops the final E, and 'mobbed by' has the shortened comparative crowd round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors are soldiers or combatants, hence fighters.

clue.text: God, universal god, recalling what he represents

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Ra represents the sun

explanation.surface: A deity is described by another god's associations.
explanation.walkthrough: Ra represents the sun; 'recalling' turns SUN into NUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek personification of the sky, father of the Titans, so a god.

clue.text: Radio report's latest broadcast

parts.note: a report can be a cry or shout, plus the 's

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The newest news report goes out over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An early simple wireless receiver using a crystal detector, a type of radio.

clue.text: Describing ball in second movie involving that woman

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the film holds the pronoun inside

parts.note: pic is slang for a film
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: In a film sequel, a woman appears in a scene about a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance, but it means a round shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheric means round or globe-shaped, the adjective for describing a ball.

clue.text: Kinky sex: an unpleasant notion for kids?

parts.note: S and M, sadomasochism, is a kinky sexual practice

explanation.surface: A warning that racy sex is no thing for children.
explanation.walkthrough: S AND M (sadomasochism) is spelt out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The folklore figure who sprinkles sand to send children to sleep: bedtime, an unwelcome idea to youngsters.

clue.text: Reduced opening on jug — repairman perhaps here

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a rent is a tear or opening
a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: A cracked jug spout sends someone to the repair shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is a closing link pointing to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who restores worn things to good condition, of which a repairman is one example.

clue.text: Attention is absorbed by a lot of females of limited attraction?

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside, so these letters go within the other piece
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: women are females
to give an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A man's attention is captured by many women who are not very alluring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome and dull, so something with little appeal or interest.

clue.text: Important conclusions from work force survey

indicators.note: conclusions from means the closing letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A workforce study yields significant findings.
explanation.definitionFit: Key as an adjective means crucial or of great importance.

clue.text: Writer backed work of composer as No. 1 in the main

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tune is a composer's melody

explanation.surface: A writer supports a composer's piece as the top choice in general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea, not 'mainly'; the Roman sea god is chief there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of the sea rules the ocean, so is number one on the briny.

clue.text: Pointless ignoring fellow capturing one's exploit

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the trimmed word encloses the other letters
ignoring means leaving out, so the letter for fellow is dropped

parts.note: futile means pointless
one is I, and I's becomes IS

explanation.surface: A pointless man ignores a scheme he could exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, matching utilise as a verb.

clue.text: Crew is going over last of vague road markings?

indicators.note: going over means turning over, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A road crew checks unclear lines on the tarmac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns GANG IS into SIGNAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Signs collectively, including those along roads, so road markings is an example with a question mark.

clue.text: Discontented look: I'm tucking in during precursor to meal

indicators.note: tucking in during means placing inside, so the short word goes within the prayer

parts.note: grace is a prayer said before eating

explanation.surface: Someone eats greedily while the blessing is still being said, drawing a frown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking in' looks like eating, but signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted facial expression of disgust or pain, so a look of displeasure.

clue.text: My critical comments not entirely representative of weird activities

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is shown without its last letter

parts.note: stick is harsh criticism, as in getting stick

explanation.surface: Someone's harsh remarks only partly reflect odd goings-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer or occultist practises the supernatural, so stands for strange spiritual activities.

clue.text: Male aboard light boat mostly going at low speed

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so the letter goes inside the vessel
mostly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a sloop is a light single-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A man on a small sailing boat cruises slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow motion, the film technique, describes something proceeding at a reduced pace.

clue.text: Wizard publication here in France, with covers from American

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication
ici is French for here

indicators.note: covers from means the outer letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A magazine about sorcery published in France with American cover art.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard is a sorcerer or conjuror, a synonym in the sense of one who does magic.

clue.text: Weak upturns after investment by Government? A dark time

indicators.note: investment means placing inside, so the letter is wrapped in the other piece
upturns means turns upside down, which in a down clue reverses the word

parts.note: thin can mean weak, as in a thin argument

explanation.surface: A weak economy recovers after state investment, though the outlook stays grim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' suggests finance but means enclosing: 'upturns' makes NIHT, which takes in G.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness between dusk and dawn, so a dark time.

clue.text: Equivalent pages in middle of book

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the abbreviation sits within the middle letters
middle of means the central letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Matching pages sit at the centre of a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for one's counterpart or opposite number, so an equivalent person.

clue.text: No security organisation will bring in a woman

indicators.note: bring in means take inside, so the letter goes within the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
MI stands for Military Intelligence, as in MI5

explanation.surface: A spy agency refuses to recruit a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical female name, so the answer is a woman by example.

clue.text: Leave us and Henry beset by bad smell

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the stink encloses the other letters

parts.note: pong is British slang for a stink
Hal is a nickname for Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Someone tells their companion Henry to get away from a terrible stench.
explanation.definitionFit: To get moving and depart, so a phrasal verb meaning to go off.

clue.text: Fellow securing work on castle outside historic city to display positive attitude

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the pronoun encloses the next piece

parts.note: he refers to a fellow
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the stronghold goes round the city

parts.note: a fort is a fortified castle
Thebes is an ancient city of Greece and Egypt

explanation.surface: A man works on a castle near an ancient city, staying upbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: An optimistic idiom meaning to stay hopeful that things will turn out well.
